title: Students protest RSS leader's presence at Central University of Kerala event
seoTitle: Kasaragod students protest RSS leader's presence

tea.why: Students protested the presence of an RSS-linked leader at a university seminar and alleged an attempt to advance a 'saffronisation agenda'.
tea.want: Protesters demanded that universities provide equal space for all ideological viewpoints and not be used for political agendas.
tea.changed: Oct 6: Four students were reportedly injured during clashes with police at the university campus.

summary: Students from various organizations, including KSU, MSF, SFI, NSUI, and AISF, protested at the Central University of Kerala in Kasaragod on October 6. They opposed the presence of J. Nandakumar, national convener of an RSS-linked organization, at a seminar on 'Vande Mataram'. Protesters alleged an attempt to promote a 'saffronisation agenda' and claimed some registered students were denied entry. Police were present at the venue, preventing students from entering the hall. Clashes reportedly occurred between students and police, resulting in four student injuries.
demands: Oppose the presence of J. Nandakumar at the seminar
Oppose Akhil Bharatiya Sahitya Parishad as a co-organiser
Universities should provide equal space to all ideological viewpoints
Universities should not be turned into platforms for political agendas
Allow registered students entry to the program
response: Police maintained a heavy presence at the venue and prevented protesting students from entering the seminar hall. Students alleged that police assaulted them during confrontations. A university official stated he was unaware why registered students were denied entry.

injuries.text: Four students were reportedly injured during clashes between the police and student protesters

updates.text: Students protested at the Central University of Kerala against the presence of an RSS-linked leader at a seminar.
Protesters also objected to being denied entry to the event despite having registered.
Police prevented students from entering the seminar hall, leading to confrontations.
Four students were reportedly injured during clashes with police on the university campus.
